title: for loops
learningGoals: write the three parts of a for loop

youtube.title: C++ for Loop: Count with Confidence | C++ Programming EP 17
youtube.description: In this episode you will write the three parts of a for loop, count up and down and spot an empty loop body, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 for loops · 0:53 Count the rounds · 1:33 Three parts, one loop · 2:03 Second program · 3:03 Recap · 3:37 Bug of the Day · 4:25 Challenge · 4:45 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "FOR LOOP" in tomato on cream; Xecxec next to a counter with a start, a stop and a step; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a counter with a start, a stop and a step

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we meet the for loop. It packs the start, the test and the step into one tidy line.

scenes.onScreen: "for loops": numbered lines (1. Start, test and step live in one line; 2. The body runs once per round; 3. The loop variable belongs to the loop) and an analogy card: a bus route: start at the first stop, check each stop, move to the next
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A for loop has three parts in its round brackets. First, the start. It runs once. Second, the test. It runs before each round. Third, the step. It runs after each round. A variable made in the start belongs only to the loop. Think of a bus route. You begin at the first stop, check if there is a next stop, and move on.
points: Start, test and step live in one line
The body runs once per round
The loop variable belongs to the loop

analogy.title: for loops
analogy.body: A bus route: start at the first stop, check each stop, move to the next

scenes.onScreen: rounds.cpp: a for loop prints five rounds
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 5] The start makes i equal to one. The test checks that i is at most five. The step adds one to i. [HL 6] The body prints the round number. [TRACK i=1] Round one prints one. [TRACK i=2] Then i becomes two, and the body runs again. [TRACK i=6] When i is six, the test fails, and the loop ends.

scenes.onScreen: a flow: start, test, body, step
scenes.animation: Steps drop in left to right with a pop; connecting arrows draw on; the active step glows butter
scenes.narration: Here is the order. The start runs once. Then the test runs. If it is true, the body runs, and then the step runs. After the step, the test runs again. This repeats until the test is false.

diagram.caption: a flow: start, test, body, step

scenes.onScreen: tableseven.cpp: a for loop prints seven times one to five
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 6] The body prints one row of the table. The loop makes five rows. [HL 8] A second loop counts down. It starts at three. The step is k minus minus. [HL 9] It prints three, two and one. [HL 11] Then endl ends the line.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as tableseven dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The table of seven prints five rows. Then the line, three two one, appears.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. A for loop holds the start, the test and the step in one line. Two. The start runs once, and the step runs after each round. Three. Count down with minus minus. Four. Never put a semicolon after the closing round bracket. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: A for loop holds the start, the test and the step in one line.
The start runs once, and the step runs after each round.
Never put a semicolon after the closing round bracket.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: A semicolon after the for
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; the g++ warning appears in tomato; the fix slides in and the warning goes away with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. A semicolon sits after the for line. That is an empty body. The loop spins five times and does nothing. Then the block runs only once. The compiler warns about the empty body. Remove the semicolon.

scenes.onScreen: Why do for loops make good friends? They always count on you.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: Why do for loops make good friends? They always count on you.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: print a triangle of numbers
scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Use a for loop to print the even numbers from two to twenty. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: range-based for loops. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Compiler output (a warning, the program still builds):

rounds.cpp: In function 'int main()':
rounds.cpp:5:5: warning: this 'for' clause does not guard... [-Wmisleading-indentation]
    5 |     for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++);
      |     ^~~
rounds.cpp:6:5: note: ...this statement, but the latter is misleadingly indented as if it were guarded by the 'for'
    6 |     {
bug.why: The semicolon is an empty loop body. The loop runs five times and does nothing. The block below then runs once.

pun: "Why do for loops make good friends? They always count on you."
challenge: Use a for loop to print the even numbers from two to twenty.
challengeAnswer: Start i at two. Test i at most twenty. Step i by two, using i plus equals two.
